summary: Equinox Systems is evaluating Redwood for an LLM feature in their customer support product. They want details on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SDK support (Python/JS), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy options for rate limiting and observability hooks. Agreed to run a 2-week POC with benchmarking; Redwood to send pricing and integration examples.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-02
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE); Oliver Reed (Equinox CTO); Priya Shah (Lead ML Engineer); Samir Khan (Platform Engineer)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Carlos from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Oliver: Doing good, thanks. Excited to talk through integration options — we've been evaluating a few vendors and want to understand how Redwood would fit our infra.
[00:14] Priya: Yeah, hi, Priya here. I'm mainly focused on model quality and orchestration — how you'd hook in to our prompt pipelines, LangChain, LlamaIndex, that sort of thing.
[00:24] Carlos: Great — that's right up our alley. Quick agenda: we'll cover Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SDKs and connectors, gateway/proxy and rate limiting, and observability hooks. Then we'll recap next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Samir: Sounds good. We'll also flag security/network questions as we go.
[00:36] Maya: Perfect. Oliver, can you give a quick 2-minute overview of the product you want to add?
[00:40] Oliver: Sure. We're building a semi-automated support assistant that ingests tickets and suggests replies, plus a summarization feed for managers. Latency matters — sub 500ms P95 ideally for reply suggestions — and we have roughly 120 QPS peak across global regions, currently routed via our gateway. Data residency in EU is a requirement for some customers.
[01:03] Priya: Also we need to integrate with our retriever stack — we use LlamaIndex for doc indexing, LangChain orchestration in Python for prompt templating. We want Redwood to be as drop-in as possible there.
[01:12] Carlos: Got it. On latency/cost tradeoffs: Hosted is simplest and fastest to get running, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit costs at scale, and Private gives full network control and compliance. For 120 QPS and 500ms P95, Dedicated is a common recommendation, but we can benchmark Hosted first.
[01:33] Maya: Quick question — are you planning to do streaming responses for the reply editor, or full completion then display?
[01:38] Priya: We'll probably stream partial tokens for editor UX, then finalize.
[01:42] Samir: And we'll need to enforce per-customer quotas; we can't have a single noisy tenant blow the budget. So gateway-level rate limits that map to our tenant IDs are critical.
[01:51] Carlos: Good note. Redwood supports per-api-key and per-route quotas; with Dedicated/Private you get more granular rate-limits on the gateway. We also have a sidecar-style proxy for on-prem that allows token tagging for billing and per-tenant throttles.
[02:07] Oliver: When you say "sidecar proxy" do you mean we have to run something, or is that optional?
[02:12] Carlos: It's optional. For Hosted you can use our cloud gateway with header-based tenant mapping; for Private/on-prem you can deploy our gateway/proxy as a small container that sits in front of requests. It supports JWT, mTLS, and integrates with your existing API gateway.
[02:25] Priya: How are SDKs? We prefer Python for LangChain and JavaScript for frontend. Do you have adapters?
[02:31] Maya: Yes, we have official SDKs for Python and JS. Carlos, do you want to call out LangChain/LlamaIndex examples?
[02:37] Carlos: Sure — we maintain example repos. For LangChain we provide a connector (llm wrapper) that respects streaming, function calling, and token limits. For LlamaIndex we have retriever examples that show using our embeddings endpoint alongside a local index. There are minor naming mismatches sometimes in the autogenerated docs, we've seen that in older transcriptions — but we keep examples up to date.
[02:58] Priya: Nice. For embeddings, are you recommending we use Redwood embeddings or keep our own? We use a hybrid approach today.
[03:05] Carlos: You can use Redwood embeddings; for privacy-sensitive data many customers generate embeddings in their VPC (Private) and use only the service for model inference. We also support bringing-your-own-embeddings with no additional charges.
[03:17] Oliver: On the observability side — we need tracing correlation from our request IDs through your platform, and per-request latency/ token counts in our metrics (Prometheus) plus logs for audits. What's available?
[03:28] Carlos: We emit per-request metrics and traces; integrations with Datadog, NewRelic, and Prometheus are available. For Private deployments you can forward logs to your ELK stack and enable audit logs that include token-level counts and KMS key IDs for crypto ops.
[03:42] Samir: And for SOC 2/ISO, can we get the compliance package? We'll need an SOC2 attestation and details on key management.
[03:50] Maya: Absolutely — I'll attach our compliance pack and the SOC2 report. For KMS: Hosted supports Redwood-managed KMS by default; Dedicated and Private can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) and we provide logs of key usage.
[04:04] Priya: Regarding rate limits, can we set per-tenant burst windows and per-route token caps? For example, support-replies route gets higher concurrency than summarization.
[04:14] Carlos: Yes — per-route and per-api-key limits are configurable. We also have a quota enforcement layer that supports burst tokens and sliding windows, and you can attach webhook callbacks on limit hits for observability or policy enforcement.
[04:28] Oliver: One concern: prefix/KV cache behavior — our retriever often hits the same docs; we want to minimize repeated KV cache warmups when doing multi-turn. How is caching handled?
[04:39] Carlos: We do KV cache across requests on the runtime; Dedicated and Private have deterministic cache residency options. For Hosted we do best-effort caching but due to multi-tenant isolation the warmup characteristics can vary. For predictable multi-turn throughput, Dedicated or Private is recommended because you control the GPU pool and cache affinity.
[04:58] Priya: About integration complexity — do we need to rewrite prompts or is there a compatibility layer? We use LangChain's prompt templates heavily.
[05:05] Carlos: No rewrite needed; our SDKs accept plain text prompts and also support function calls and structured outputs. LangChain wrapper just calls our endpoint; you can pass the prompt templates unchanged. We do recommend adding guardrails for token usage and to use our streaming client to improve UX.
[05:20] Maya: Do you have a timeline and success criteria for POC?
[05:22] Oliver: We'd like to run a 2-week POC to evaluate latency P95, cost per 1k tokens, and qualitative quality compared to our internal baseline. Decision by end of month.
[05:33] Maya: Great. We'll propose POC gates and a benchmark plan. Carlos will run the technical setup and test vectors.
[05:38] Samir: Network-wise, if we run Hosted, traffic will go over the public internet; for EU data residency we might need to use a regional Dedicated or Private. Can you guarantee region pins?
[05:48] Carlos: Yes — Dedicated and Private support region pinning; Hosted can be pinned to EU regions as well but there are data residency notes which we'll share. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[05:58] Priya: About cost — do you have guidance on quantization or model variants for cost reduction? We might be fine with a slightly lower quality model for summarization.
[06:08] Carlos: We provide model profiles and quantization recommendations per workload. For summarization, a quantized 4-bit variant can be very cost-effective. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions automatically based on token distribution and latency targets.
[06:20] Oliver: Perfect. For the gateway/proxy, is there an out-of-the-box integration with Kong/Apigee, or do we have to use your sidecar?
[06:29] Carlos: We have adapters for common API gateways and the proxy can run as a sidecar or standalone container. The adapter maps headers for tenant-id, trace id, and enforces rate limits at the gateway layer.
[06:40] Priya: Any limitations on streaming + function calling with LangChain? We've had issues with interleaved function calls before.
[06:47] Carlos: Our streaming supports chunked function-call events; the LangChain wrapper has been updated to handle interleaved calls. Some older SDK versions had bugs — we'll share a tested example.
[06:57] Maya: Quick pause — I want to surface a few common pitfalls: 1) mixing hosted default keys with high-volume tenants can cause cost surprises; 2) assuming cache behaviors are identical across Hosted/Dedicated; and 3) not instrumenting token counts end-to-end. We'll include docs on all three.
[07:13] Oliver: Good call. On security — what's the SSO story? We use SAML with Okta and need RBAC for internal users.
[07:20] Maya: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC; RBAC roles include Admin, Dev, Viewer, and Ops. For Private we can sync with your IdP for provisioning.
[07:29] Samir: For audit logs we need immutable logs for 1 year at EU retention. Is that supported?
[07:34] Carlos: Yes — audit log retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can provide logs but retention limits apply to shared tenants; we can discuss extended retention as an add-on.
[07:45] Priya: Any latency overhead with the proxy/sidecar? We want minimal added RTT.
[07:50] Carlos: It's lightweight — typically a few ms added per request. The main latency drivers are model size, sequence length, and batching. We can surface expected P95 in the benchmark.
[07:59] Oliver: Can you explain batching behavior? We have occasional spikes and then idle windows. We don't want large batching to add tail latency.
[08:08] Carlos: The runtime does continuous batching with latency SLOs; you define per-route latency targets and the runtime will serve smaller batches to meet P95. There's also CPU/GPU kernel selection based on sequence length. We can show sample profiles.
[08:23] Maya: Let's talk about integration process: Carlos will onboard your SE to the repo, provide sandbox keys, and the LangChain/LlamaIndex example code. We'll also run a small benchmark test against a test model.
[08:33] Priya: Do you need data to run quality tests? We can provide a small sample set of anonymized tickets.
[08:37] Carlos: That would be ideal — anonymized is fine. For quality we'll run the same prompt set you use in production if possible.
[08:43] Oliver: Regarding billing, how granular are invoices? We need per-team breakdowns and per-tenant chargebacks.
[08:50] Maya: Billing for Dedicated can be split by API key tags; we can provide usage exports that map to your tenant IDs. Hosted also supports usage tagging but dedicated gives clearer unit economics.
[08:59] Samir: For POC, do you allow temporary higher quotas? Our test might simulate 300 QPS briefly.
[09:05] Carlos: Yes — we can provision burst capacity for the POC on Dedicated, and we can simulate on Hosted depending on availability. We'll work with infra to provision a test window.
[09:15] Priya: Slightly tangential — do you support model rollouts and canarying across model versions? We want to test different model sizes.
[09:23] Carlos: Redwood Console supports rollouts and A/B testing with automatic fallback. You can pin per-route model variants and we support gradual traffic shifts.
[09:31] Oliver: Perfect. Any constraints around function calling with structured outputs and downstream parsers?
[09:37] Carlos: We have structured output support and schema enforcement; the SDKs validate outputs and the console can run regression checks against your eval sets.
[09:46] Maya: Okay, let's jump into some rough POC plan bullets — I'll read them and you tell me if anything's missing. 1) Redwood provides sandbox keys + example repo; 2) Equinox supplies anonymized dataset and traffic profile; 3) Run 2-week benchmark for latency/cost/quality; 4) Weekly check-in with SE; 5) Final decision meeting.
[10:09] Oliver: That covers it. Any legal/procurement timing we should be aware of?
[10:13] Maya: Standard NDA in place? If you want SOC2 early we can share it now. Procurement timelines vary but for Dedicated we usually see a 4-6 week procurement cycle after POC for enterprise accounts.
[10:23] Samir: We'll loop in legal if POC outcomes are positive.
[10:26] Priya: A couple of technical nitty-grittys — for LangChain we use async clients; your Python SDK is async?
[10:32] Carlos: Yes, our Python SDK has sync and async clients. The streaming client is async-first but we have patterns for sync wrappers.
[10:41] Priya: Great. Also, LlamaIndex — any recommendations for embedding dimensionality? We currently use 1536 dims.
[10:48] Carlos: 1536 is common; embedding provider selection is workload-dependent. For retrieval-heavy pipelines we recommend dense vectors plus FAISS/Retrieval with caching on the index side. We'll enumerate options in the integration guide.
[11:00] Oliver: Before we wrap, can you confirm what you'll send after this call?
[11:03] Maya: Sure: 1) Pricing + TCO spreadsheet for Dedicated and Hosted scenarios; 2) Compliance pack (SOC2, encryption/KMS docs); 3) LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo link; 4) POC benchmark plan. I'll email those today.
[11:20] Carlos: I'll share the sandbox keys and a short runbook for the sidecar proxy plus an example for per-tenant rate-limits.
[11:30] Priya: We'll prepare the anonymized tickets and traffic profile and send them by Friday.
[11:35] Oliver: Ok good. Anything else?
[11:37] Maya: Quick FYI — when you look at the examples, watch for minor auto-transcription name mismatches; also the SDK doc generation sometimes introduces outdated function names — Carlos will point to the right branch.
[11:47] Samir: Thanks.
[11:49] Maya: Recap of action items and owners: Maya to send pricing and compliance, Carlos to share code and sandbox, Priya and Samir to send data and network diagram. We'll target POC start next week pending schedules.
[11:59] Oliver: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:02] (meeting end)
